role.altitude: The oral surgeon keeps examining, reading images, treating and planning with colleagues; typing notes, letters and lab orders shrinks.
skills_to_grow: Checking scribe drafts and draft letters
role.ambitious_version: A surgeon whose notes and letters are done before the next patient.

tasks.short: Read the referral letter, examine the patient's mouth, read the panoramic X-ray or CBCT, discuss findings and options with the patient, write the consultation note and write, check and send the reply to the referring dentist to evaluate the position of the wisdom teeth.

steps.what: Surgeon reads the referral letter
Surgeon examines the patient's mouth
Surgeon evaluates the position of the wisdom teeth and nerve proximity on the X-ray or CBCT
Surgeon discusses findings and options with the patient
Surgeon writes the consultation note

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent.
loop.output: A draft clinical note in the record's sections.
loop.check: The surgeon reads each draft against the exam findings and what was agreed with the patient, corrects it, and writes the note by hand when the draft misses or changes a finding.
loop.stop: Consultations without consent are written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Findings are spoken in free conversation.

steps.what: Surgeon writes the reply letter to the referring dentist

loop.input: The saved clinical note and the referrer's question.
loop.output: A draft letter quoting the note sections it uses.
loop.check: The surgeon reads each draft against the saved note: findings, advice and urgency must match the note; when the note is incomplete the letter is written by hand.
loop.stop: Complex cases are written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each letter answers a different question.

steps.what: Surgeon checks the final letter: findings and advice match the note, and the addressee is the referring dentist; then signs it
Surgeon sends the signed letter to the referring dentist

approvals.approved_version: The reply letter exactly as checked and signed by the surgeon in s7, sent once to the referring dentist; any change needs a new signature.

tasks.design: With the patient's consent, a certified scribe drafts the consultation note from the recorded consultation and the surgeon corrects it before saving; the reply letter starts from a draft built from the saved note, which the surgeon edits, signs and sends. Examining, reading the images and talking with the patient stay with the surgeon.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes and letters were typed after each patient.
tasks.human_edge: Judging nerve risk on a CBCT.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates the note before it goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (29%) across 236,153 scribe notes.
Tandem's scribe and coding carry MDR class IIa.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating wisdom teeth; the extraction itself is outside.
The note step keeps 71, applying the 29% per-note time cut from the Capio case; that case was self-estimated and partly vendor-authored. Each task's own note is counted once, in its own task.
s6 keeps 70: the draft takes the patient details, findings and layout from the saved note, but the surgeon still rewrites the advice in each letter.
The means prior puts 74% in person; the steps show 55%, because image reading and writing take 45%.
research_questions: Do notes take less time without omissions?

incremental.description: Oral surgeon asks each patient for consent to record and handles refusals.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of patients decline recording, so half of notes are typed as today and s5 keeps 86 (2.6); high: most patients consent and s5 keeps 71 as in the Capio case (4.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read referrals and records from the orthodontist, plan treatment jointly, review 3D scans and the virtual surgical plan, write, check and send the joint treatment plan letter, phone colleagues to coordinate timing and attend multidisciplinary meetings to collaborate with dentists and orthodontists on treatment.

steps.what: Surgeon reads referrals and records from the orthodontist
Surgeon collaborates with restorative dentists and orthodontists to plan treatment
Surgeon reviews 3D scans and the virtual surgical plan
Surgeon writes the joint treatment plan letter

loop.input: The saved clinical note and the referrer's question.
loop.output: A draft letter quoting the note sections it uses.
loop.check: The surgeon reads each draft against the joint plan and the reviewed surgical plan: each step, side and timing must match, and quoted sections must say what the letter claims; unclear drafts are rewritten by hand.
loop.stop: Complex cases are written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each letter answers a different question.

steps.what: Surgeon checks the final letter: the plan, timing and named colleagues match the joint plan; then signs it
Surgeon sends the signed letter to the treating colleagues
Surgeon phones and mails colleagues to coordinate timing
Surgeon attends multidisciplinary meetings

approvals.approved_version: The treatment plan letter exactly as checked and signed by the surgeon in s5, sent once to the named colleagues; any change needs a new signature.

tasks.design: The joint treatment plan letter starts from a draft built from the saved notes and plan, quoting the sections it uses; the surgeon edits, signs and sends it. Reading records, joint planning, reviewing scans, coordination calls and meetings stay with the surgeon.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing the order of surgery and braces.
assumptions: Boundary: collaborating on treatment plans; the surgery itself is outside.
s4 keeps 75: the draft fills patient details, records and the plan sections from saved notes, but the reasoning of each joint plan is written by the surgeon.
The means prior puts 69% in person; the steps show 51%, because records, scans, letters and sending take 37%.
No new work: the draft runs on notes and plans that are saved today; checking the draft is inside s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: joint plans are mostly free text that the draft cannot take over, so s4 keeps 90 (1.0); high: the draft takes details and plan sections as designed, s4 keeps 75 (2.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the history and examine the jaw, review imaging, explain the diagnosis and treatment, treat temporomandibular joint problems with injections, splints or surgery, write the clinical note and fill in, check and send the splint order to the lab to evaluate and treat TMJ problems.

steps.what: Surgeon takes the history and evaluates the temporomandibular joint
Surgeon reviews joint imaging
Surgeon explains the diagnosis and treatment options
Surgeon treats the problem with injections, splint fitting or surgery
Surgeon writes the clinical note

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent.
loop.output: A draft clinical note in the record's sections.
loop.check: The surgeon reads each draft against the history, the exam and the treatment given, corrects it, and writes the note by hand when the draft misses or changes a finding.
loop.stop: Consultations without consent are written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Findings are spoken in free conversation.

steps.what: Surgeon fills in the splint order, typing patient details and attaching scans by hand
Surgeon checks the final splint order: patient, splint design, attached scan and the named lab
Surgeon sends the approved order to the dental lab

approvals.approved_version: The splint order with scans exactly as checked by the surgeon in s7, sent once to the named lab; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: With consent, a certified scribe drafts the clinical note and the surgeon corrects it before saving. The splint order fills patient details from the record and attaches the scan, instead of typing them. History, examination, imaging, explaining, treatment, the order check and sending stay with the surgeon.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes and orders were typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified scribes and lab orders linked to the record.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether pain is joint or muscle.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation and the clinician validates the note before it goes into the record.
At Capio Ramsay Santé, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (29%) across 236,153 scribe notes.
Tandem's scribe and coding carry MDR class IIa.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating and treating TMJ problems; wisdom tooth evaluation (task 9372 in this set) is a separate task with its own note.
The note step keeps 71, applying the 29% per-note time cut from the Capio case; that case was self-estimated and partly vendor-authored. Each task's own note is counted once, in its own task.
s6 keeps half because the splint design is written by hand.
The means prior puts 76% in person; the steps show 72%, the same picture.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of patients decline recording (s5 keeps 86) and the scan often has to be attached by hand (s6 keeps 75) (1.9); high: most consent and the order fills from the record (4.4).
